rows.threat: An attacker uses a stolen or guessed password to log in as a legitimate user, because local email/password login remains available alongside SSO and isn't covered by MFA.
rows.current_mitigation: SSO is enforced for the main application, but three legacy service accounts still use local password auth with no MFA (per admin interview).

rows.threat: An admin-level attacker disables audit log export to the SIEM, allowing their subsequent actions to go undetected and unattributed.
rows.current_mitigation: Audit logs are exported to Splunk via the vendor's native integration; no alert currently fires if the export stops (per admin interview).

rows.threat: A compromised standard-user account is granted admin-level permissions by another compromised or malicious admin account, with no second approval required.
rows.current_mitigation: No approval workflow exists for permission or role changes; any admin can unilaterally grant roles (per admin interview).
